subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Watt's Separate Condenser: The Efficiency Leap
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Watt's Separate Condenser: The Efficiency Leap.

hook.text: James Watt asked: why cool the cylinder if you can cool the steam elsewhere?

buildup.text: He added a separate vessel to condense steam while the cylinder stayed hot.

discovery.text: Fuel use dropped by 75%. The engine paid for itself in saved coal.

twist.text: Watt didn't invent the steam engine — he made it efficient enough to matter.

climax.text: His engine powered factories, mills, and mines across all of Britain.

punchline.text: One idea — keep the cylinder hot — launched the industrial age.

quiz.question: How did Watt's separate condenser improve engine efficiency?
options: It increased the steam pressure inside the cylinder
The cylinder stayed hot while steam condensed in a separate cooled vessel
It allowed the engine to run on cheaper grades of coal
